extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental investigators, and scientists seeking methodological guidance for investigating nature
extracted.subtask_description: Methodological rules for discovering forms, latent processes, and conformations in nature via ordered induction: assembling experimental/natural histories, constructing tables of instances (affirmative, negative, comparative), and performing targeted experiments rather than speculative or destructive separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary axioms / investigation of simple natures
rubrics_metrics.description: This method of operating sets out from what is constant, eternal, and universal in nature (simple natures) and opens broad paths to human power; the higher and radical operations upon nature depend entirely on the primary axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin inquiry at the level of simple, universal natures (e.g., spontaneous rotation, attraction, magnetic force). Use knowledge of these primary axioms as the genuine and clear light that dispels subtile difficulties; prioritize them when aiming at fundamental understanding or powerful change of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary axioms / investigation of latent processes
rubrics_metrics.description: A second kind of axiom depends on discovery of the latent process and proceeds by concrete bodies as found in nature and its usual course (e.g., generation of metals from menstruum, growth of plants from juices or seeds, generation of animals from coition to birth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate entire continued processes which often escape the senses. Ask detailed process-questions (what is lost, what remains, what is added, what is contracted, what unites or separates, what is continuous or broken, what urges forward or impedes, what predominates or is subservient). Recognize this method as often more prompt and promising for many inquiries, but subordinate for radical operations to primary axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent conformation / real anatomy of compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation and discovery of the latent conformation in bodies (their subtle internal texture and disposition) must be achieved; one cannot properly transform a body without complete knowledge of its latent conformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor reasoning, true induction, experiment, comparisons with other bodies, and reduction to simple natures rather than relying on crude separations (e.g., by fire) that may superinduce new natures. Examine components such as spirit, tangible essence, hairs, fibres, pores, passages, veins, cells, and the situational arrangement of these parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operative branch anchored in primary axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The operative branch extends from what is usually observed in nature to closely connected subjects, but the higher and radical operations upon nature depend entirely on primary axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying knowledge to action (technology, mechanics), use observations of usual nature for proximate operations but seek grounding in simple natures when attempting deeper or more radical transformations; do not assume operative success without such grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a complete and accurate natural and experimental history
rubrics_metrics.description: First prepare, as a foundation for the whole, a complete and accurate natural and experimental history. We must not imagine or invent, but discover the acts and properties of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect varied instances and record them carefully. Because natural history is diffuse and distracting, fix and exhibit it in due order by forming tables and coordinations so the understanding may act upon them. This is the necessary groundwork before genuine induction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form tables of existence / presence (affirmative instances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present to the understanding all the known instances which agree in the same nature (a mere history, without premature reflection or too great refinement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile a 'Table of Existence and Presence' listing many exemplars of the phenomenon (Bacon's example: a long list of instances exhibiting heat). Avoid premature theorizing while assembling this affirmative table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form tables of deviation / proximate negatives (absence in proximity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present instances which do not admit of the given nature; the want of the given nature must be inquired into more particularly in objects which have a very close connection with those others in which it is present and manifest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a 'Table of Deviation' or 'Absence in Proximity' by classing negatives under affirmatives and focusing on near or closely related cases rather than every possible negative. Use proximate negatives to constrain and refine the form (e.g., lunar rays not warm to touch).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form tables of degrees / comparative instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit instances in which the nature is present in greater or less degree—compare its increase and decrease in the same object or among different objects—since the form must uniformly diminish and increase with the given nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble a 'Table of Degrees' to test whether the putative form co-varies with the phenomenon. Use degrees across materials, organisms, organs, and circumstances (e.g., comparative heat across animals, parts of animals, and inanimate bodies).

rubrics_metrics.name: True and legitimate induction as the key
rubrics_metrics.description: Our third ministration must be true and legitimate induction, the very key of interpretation. The understanding, left to itself, is incompetent to construct axioms without direction and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only after careful collection and organization of instances (senses -> memory/history) should reason apply legitimate induction to derive axioms. 'Begin at the end, and go back again to the others'—use induction to ascend from tables to axioms, not from speculation to facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ministrations for eliciting axioms: senses, memory, reason
rubrics_metrics.description: The signs for interpretation of nature admit of three ministrations: (1) to the senses, (2) to the memory, (3) to the mind or reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence work: gather sensory observations (experiments), record and order them into memory/experimental history (tables), then apply reasonive induction to derive axioms. Neglecting any of these stages defeats proper interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fallacies of separation by fire and destructive procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Separation of similar bodies by distillation and solutions often shows dissimilarity of the compound by union of homogeneous parts but is attended generally with fallacy: many natures are attributed to the separate bodies as if previously existent in the compound, but are induced by fire and heat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on operations (like distillation by fire) that superinduce new qualities; prefer reasoning, induction, controlled experiments, and comparisons to reveal true latent conformation. Be wary that some experimental separations may obscure rather than reveal real internal texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted experiments to detect subtile, non-sensible effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Latent processes and many natural acts are brought about by the smallest efforts too small to strike our senses, so experiments should be devised to reveal effects not obvious to touch or sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments (e.g., lenses and thermometers to test lunar heat, confining air in sealed jars to test inherent temperature, testing burning-glass on non-luminous warm objects, trials with spices, acids, and exhalations) to make subtile processes manifest. Employ instruments and indirect indicators when senses fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze processes by temporal and causal questions
rubrics_metrics.description: In all generations and transformations we must inquire: what is in the act of being lost and escaping, what remains, what is being added, what is being diluted, what is being contracted, what is being united, what is being separated, what is continuous, what is broken off, what is urging forward, what impedes, what predominates, what is subservient, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically interrogate processes along these dimensions to map causal sequence and agent roles. Use such interrogative schema as a checklist when reconstructing latent processes and their governing causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply mathematics and prefer reduction to simple, commensurable elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigation of nature is best conducted when mathematics are applied to physics; transfer attention from the complicated to the simple, from the incommensurable to the commensurable, from the indefinite to the definite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce complex natural phenomena to simpler, quantifiable elements where possible; do not be deterred by large numbers or fractions—mathematical description clarifies and enables rigorous investigation.
